title: align-reauth-to-heartbeat-add-typed-stream-decorators-and-bump-sdks
author: Maya Chen
commits: feat: introduce heartbeat-aligned reauth scheduler and session shim
feat(python): async iterator decorator for resilient streaming consumers
feat(ts): add typed async generator decorators + examples
feat(go): define StreamHandler interface + resilient reconnect helper
test: add unit/integration tests for reauth timing and stream decorators
description:
Context and motivation: Several customer incidents showed token refreshs firing independently of the streaming heartbeat, which caused unnecessary reauth churn on long-lived streaming sessions. At the same time, language SDKs lacked a small set of ergonomically-consistent stream helpers that made consumer code resilient to brief reauth windows and restartable on transient transport errors. This PR introduces a small session shim that aligns reauth scheduling to the connection heartbeat (reduces mid-stream churn), plus typed stream decorators for Python/TypeScript and a StreamHandler pattern for Go.

What this PR does (single-string body): - Introduces heartbeat-aligned reauth scheduler: schedules refresh attempts in a jittered window relative to the latest successful heartbeat, and stalls aggressive refresh attempts if a stream heartbeat indicates the session is active. This reduces unnecessary credential swaps during healthy streams. - Adds Python async decorator @resilient_stream to wrap AsyncIterator/AsyncGenerator consumers with transparent reattach+resume semantics and exponential backoff profiles. - Adds TypeScript typed async generator decorators (resilientGenerator) with streaming-friendly retry presets and a small examples folder. - Adds Go StreamHandler interface + resilient reconnect helper that encapsulates credential refresh hooks and backoff wiring. - Bumps SDK versions: python -> 2.5.0 (minor), typescript -> 1.13.0, go -> v1.9.2. - Tests: unit and integration tests covering scheduling windows and stream decorator resume semantics. - Docs: migration guide and small examples demonstrating patterns.

Checklist: - [x] Design review (ENG-5123) - [x] Unit tests for scheduler and decorators - [x] Integration tests against ephemeral testbed - [x] Docs + migration guide - [x] SDK version bumps and release notes - [x] CI green (some flaky tests retried)

Commit summary (high level): feat: add scheduler/sessions shim; feat: language-specific stream helpers; chore: sdk bumps; test/docs. See commits array for messages.

Files changed (high level): See changed_files array; main functional changes are under sdk/* and docs/examples. The session shim is in sdk/*/cred/scheduler and the language helpers are under their respective streaming/ directories.

Review conversation summary: - Anders flagged a potential race between heartbeat updates and background refresh; I added a compare-and-update guard and extended unit tests to cover concurrent heartbeat pings. - Priya asked to normalize retry presets across languages; added a shared presets table and documented differences in the migration guide. - Diego requested stronger logs at INFO level for refresh attempts; added structured logs to Python and TS helpers and a traced span in Go.

CI: Full matrix run (py/ts/go) initially had two flaky integration tests on the TS generator; reran and they passed. All checks green at merge time.

Migration notes: Consumers using long-lived streams should prefer the new decorators/handler. For Python: decorate your async generator with @resilient_stream(backoff_profile='conservative') and remove manual reauth scheduling. For TS: wrap your async generator via resilientGenerator(...) helper. For Go: implement the StreamHandler interface and use stream.ReconnectWrap to get automatic reconnect and credential refresh coordination.

Why this change is safe: Scheduler defaults preserve previous refresh frequency for non-streaming sessions; stream-aligned behavior is opt-in via the new SessionConfig.wait_for_heartbeat flag (default true for streaming helpers). SDK bumps are minor and do not change runtime APIs except for the addition of these helpers and a small credential scheduler option.

Merge outcome: squash and merge.
review_comments: Anders Holt: Can heartbeat updates and the refresh ticker race? If the heartbeat arrives while a refresh is in flight we could be renewing unnecessarily.
Maya Chen (author): Added a compare-and-set on the session.last_heartbeat timestamp and short-circuiting if last_heartbeat > refresh_start_time. Added unit test test_concurrent_heartbeat_refresh.
Priya Kapoor: Please make retry presets consistent across languages and document any language-specific tradeoffs.
Maya Chen: Introduced presets.json and documented differences in docs/sdk/streaming-decorators.md. Presets are implemented as first-class objects in TS/Python and as config structs in Go.
Diego Ruiz: Add an INFO log for refresh attempts so we can correlate in prod.
Maya Chen: Added structured logs and an optional trace/span name configuration (session.trace_name).
release_notes: Introduced heartbeat-aligned reauth scheduler to reduce mid-stream credential churn; added resilient stream decorators for Python and TypeScript and a StreamHandler pattern for Go; bumped SDK versions (py 2.5.0, ts 1.13.0, go v1.9.2). See docs/sdk/upgrade-2.5.0.md for migration steps.
suggested_migration: Python: use @resilient_stream on long-lived async generators; TypeScript: wrap generators with resilientGenerator; Go: implement StreamHandler and call stream.ReconnectWrap. Update session config to opt into heartbeat-aligned refresh behavior if you rely on manual refresh scheduling.
